# 2 Baruch Chapter 10 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 10:1 — "Blessed is the one who was not born"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Blessed is-the-one-who-was-not-born" | Literal macarism |
| LOGOS | "Blessed is the one who was not born" | Formal macarism |
| PNEUMA | "Better never to have been born" | "Better" for "blessed" — comparative rather than beatitude |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The macarism form ("blessed is...") is deliberate — it inverts the birth-blessing convention of the psalms. PNEUMA's "better" is a comparative that loses the ironic beatitude structure.

---

## 10:3 — Mythological mourners

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sirens...night-spectres...demons and jackals" | Literal; preserves mythological vocabulary |
| LOGOS | "sirens...night-spectres...demons and jackals" | Formal; same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "sirens of the sea...night-spirits...demons and jackals" | Adds "of the sea" to sirens; "spirits" for "spectres" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Sirens from the sea" (with preposition) is already in the Syriac; PNEUMA rightly renders this. "Night-spectres" preferred over PNEUMA's "night-spirits" — "spectres" is more specifically visual/ghostly and appropriate to the mourning imagery.

---

## 10:15-19 — "Or why should...?" anaphora

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Full "Or why should...?" chains with literal conditionals | Mirrors Syriac anaphora |
| LOGOS | Full "Or why should...?" chains | Formal, preserves parallelism |
| PNEUMA | Compressed as short rhetorical questions without formula | Modern punch; loses parallelism |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The anaphoric "Or why should...if...?" pattern is a formal rhetorical device in the Syriac that must be preserved. PNEUMA's compression destroys the architectural structure of the lament.

---

## 10:5 — "the prophets have gone to sleep"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-prophets-have-gone-to-sleep" | Euphemism preserved literally |
| LOGOS | "the prophets have gone to sleep" | Formal euphemism |
| PNEUMA | "The prophets have fallen silent" | "Silent" for "gone to sleep" — reinterprets the euphemism |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Gone to sleep" is the standard Syriac euphemism for death, paralleling the NT usage (1 Thess 4:13 "those who have fallen asleep"). PNEUMA's "fallen silent" loses the eschatological death-sleep motif.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 4**
